item.title: Over 320 students compete in the Malta Skills Championships 2026
item.description: More than 320 competitors are taking part in the Malta Skills Championships at MCAST in Paola across 24 vocational and technical disciplines, the Ministry for Education and Sport said. Minister Byron Camilleri visited the competitions and met students, lecturers and experts involved in organising and assessing the events, often described as the national Olympics of Skills. Competitions held on 11 and 12 November continue at the Institute of Tourism Studies on 17 November with a further 22 competitors, covering fields including robotics, software development, mechatronics, welding, aircraft maintenance and graphic design.

item.title: Justice minister cites 600 convictions in defence of the Attorney General
item.description: Justice Minister Clifton Grima defended Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg by citing 600 convictions and 15 acquittals over the past two years, and said 19 of 28 jury trials in the past three years ended in convictions, with eight defendants receiving life sentences. The defence came amid public anger over the September acquittal of Yorgen Fenech in the Caruana Galizia murder case and the November acquittal of Lorin Scicluna in the killing of Lassana Cisse, with the Attorney General appealing the Fenech verdict. Abela separately warned against shooting down a fundamental democratic institution because of controversial verdicts, saying reform of how jurors are selected is not an easy question and that timing matters while cases are still before the courts.

item.title: Nationalist Party backs a basic salary for artists
item.description: Opposition leader Alex Borg said the Nationalist Party supports MEIAs proposal for a basic publicly funded salary for artists, made at a party-organised discussion on low pay, lack of recognition and limited access to cultural spaces. MEIA had proposed a defined, time-limited pilot giving regular income to professional artists in the run-up to the budget speech. The move follows comments by Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea that drew an angry reaction from artists and demands for his resignation; the minister has since said he will work to regain the sectors trust.

item.title: Foreign workers called to take part in week-long protest against Budget 2027
item.description: TCN Alliance Malta has launched the Green Ribbon Project, calling on third-country nationals to boycott public transport and shops from Monday, stay at home on Friday and end the week with a protest concert in Valletta against Budget 2027 measures. Patricia Garam said the campaign is a peaceful but undeniable confrontation with policies that pushed workers to a breaking point. The group said some foreign workers are reluctant to take part publicly because they fear possible repercussions.

item.title: Foreign workers called on to join week-long protest against Budget 2027
item.description: Third-country nationals have been urged to boycott public transport and shops from Monday, stay at home on Friday and end the week with a protest concert in Valletta against Budget 2027 measures that remove free public transport and childcare eligibility for those without long-term residency. The campaign, named the Green Ribbon Project and run by TCN Alliance, Solidarjetà, Moviment Graffitti and TCNs United, runs through Saturday 21 November, with a gathering and concert called United Against Discrimination due to begin at 4pm at Tritons Square. Organisers said some workers are reluctant to protest publicly because they fear possible repercussions.

item.title: PN backs a basic salary for artists after criticism of the culture sector
item.description: Nationalist Party leader Alex Borg said the party supports the Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association proposal for a basic publicly funded salary for artists, made during a party-organised discussion with creatives that was held behind closed doors after an introductory address. The MEIA proposal, put forward in the run-up to the budget, would launch a defined, time-limited pilot providing regular income to professional artists and cultural practitioners. Borg argued Malta should build a creative economy on the lines of Irelands, and called for more theatrical and creative spaces for the public, including the partys PORT cultural district proposal.

item.title: Local plans must change, Abela says, as he acknowledges population concerns
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said Maltas local plans must be revised because the framework introduced in 2006 has left a sour taste, insisting he has a strong mandate to take difficult decisions on planning. Speaking to journalists from Malta Daily, Lovin Malta and Whos Who, he acknowledged public concerns about population growth and pressure on schools and hospitals from foreign workers, saying the country needs foreign labour but not in excessive numbers. He also said the population report drafted by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana in 2018 does not form part of Cabinet records, so he cannot publish a document he does not hold, and advised those wanting it to approach its author.

item.title: Abela says local plans must change, rules out publication of Caruana population report
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela said Maltas local plans, introduced in 2006, must be revised to reflect how the country has changed, telling journalists that planning policy cannot remain static and that he has the mandate to take difficult decisions. He acknowledged public concern over population growth and the pressure foreign workers place on schools and hospitals, while insisting Malta needs foreign labour but not in excessive numbers. On third-country nationals, he said the Budget 2027 measures follow the principle that workers from outside the EU should contribute towards the public services they use, and that long-term residency processing would be improved. Abela also said the population report drafted by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana in 2018 does not form part of Cabinet records and therefore cannot be published by the government, said housing affordability remains well below levels seen in countries such as Spain, and pushed back against expectations that a light-rail project could be completed within five years while geological and viability studies continue.

item.title: Miriam Dalli reappointed as EU co-negotiator on climate adaptation at COP31
item.description: Energy, Environment and Regeneration Minister Miriam Dalli will represent the European Union at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkiye, as a negotiator on climate change adaptation. She was selected alongside the Dutch Minister to serve as co-negotiators on behalf of the EU, with the appointment announced by Ireland, which currently holds the Council of the EU Presidency. Malta will form part of a ministerial team working alongside the European Commission and member states on emissions reduction, climate finance, just transition and oceans.

item.title: Young victim of Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq boat incident undergoes successful surgery
item.description: Ben Caruana Rizzo, 14, who was found unconscious after a boat ran aground on a reef off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq a week ago, underwent successful surgery on Sunday. His father Keith Caruana, 48, died in the same incident, while a third man, Daniel Buttigieg, came out of a coma a few days later. Health Minister Ian Borg thanked the medical staff, including a surgeon who flew in for the procedure, and said the post-operative days are crucial with doctors closely monitoring the boys condition.

item.title: Animal rights group flags dog breeder keeping dogs in a residential garage
item.description: Voice for the Animals has asked the authorities to act over allegations that a number of dogs kept in the garage of a private residence are mistreated, are used for breeding and that their pups are subsequently sold. The organisation said it has made several reports to the authorities responsible for animal welfare and published a video of the premises, noting that the allegations have not been independently confirmed. MaltaToday reported the same case, saying the video shows the owner occasionally coming out to the balcony to silence the dogs.

item.title: Maltese actor Peter Galea wins best actor award in Algeria
item.description: Peter Galea won the best actor award at the second edition of the Timimoun International Short Film Festival in Algeria for his performance in the Maltese short film Unur, Fama u Glorja, written and directed by Fabrizio Fenech. The prize was presented at the festivals closing ceremony on Tuesday 10 November in Timimoun. In the film he plays Pawlu, a boxing coach whose life changes drastically after his son falls into a coma. Galea has more than 20 years of experience across theatre, television and cinema and returned to Malta in 2001.

item.title: 85% of third-country nationals surveyed call Budget 2027 measures unfair
item.description: A survey of 122 non-EU residents by Esprimi found 85% consider the Budget 2027 measures affecting them unfair and unnecessary, against 20% of Maltese respondents, with 46% saying it is unlikely they will still be living in Malta in two years. Respondents identified the new 400 annual infrastructure contribution and higher work permit fees as the measures they welcomed least, with 71% dissatisfied by each. The companion survey was conducted alongside the main poll of Maltese adults and most participants did not hold long-term residence status.

item.title: Maltese crash victim in Sicily identified as Stephania Grech, 55
item.description: The Maltese woman killed in a collision with a trailer in Sicily has been identified as Stephania Grech, 55, who was travelling alone. Witnesses quoted by Italian media said Grech took a wrong turn emerging from a motorway junction on the SiracusaGela road near Modica, and the impact hurled her car some 60 metres from the point of collision; she died at the scene. The trailer driver, a 60-year-old man from Vittoria, was left in shock and Italian authorities are investigating.

item.title: Villa Lauri in Birkirkara opens to Gozitan and nearby patients
item.description: Villa Lauri in Birkirkara has been inaugurated with its doors opened to provide accommodation and support to Gozitan patients who need to travel to Malta for medical care, and to their families. The service can be used by Gozitan residents with appointments in Malta before 10am or who need to stay overnight because of their appointment times, and by immediate family members who are eligible to accompany them.

item.title: MEIA insists it has not withdrawn its call for the arts minister to resign
item.description: The Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association has insisted it has never withdrawn its request for the resignation or removal of Arts, Culture and National Heritage Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea. item.title: Success of EU anti-cyberbullying app rests on member states, Micallefs Cabinet says
item.description: The success of the EUs planned online safety app for victims of cyberbullying will depend heavily on how national authorities adopt it, the Cabinet of Commissioner Glenn Micallef has said, with the Commission preparing to procure the tool next year. The app would let children and young people report cyberbullying to a helpline, securely store and transmit evidence and receive tailored support, and forms part of the Commissions Action Plan against cyberbullying, which contains 22 actions.

item.title: Success of EU anti-cyberbullying app will rest on member states
item.description: The Cabinet of European Commissioner Glenn Micallef said the Commissions planned online safety app for victims of cyberbullying will depend heavily on how national authorities adopt it, with the tool to be procured next year and adapted to national circumstances. The app is intended to let children and young people report cyberbullying to a helpline, securely store and transmit evidence, and receive tailored referrals to services such as law enforcement, education and child protection. It forms part of a 22-action plan funded through the Digital Europe Programme, with 1.35 million set aside for procurement.

item.title: Animal Welfare Commissioner proposes noise limits for locally made fireworks
item.description: Animal Welfare Commissioner Elliot Magro has proposed scientifically determined noise limits for locally manufactured fireworks, buffer zones around animal farms and shelters, and advance notification of displays, to protect animals from noise-related distress. The recommendations, presented to Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said, identify gaps in legislation including the absence of noise limits for local fireworks, no legally established safe distances between firing sites and animal facilities, and no official notification requirements for animal owners. Magro acknowledged fireworks are integral to Maltas cultural identity but should be balanced with safeguards.

item.title: Births to non-Maltese mothers risen from 24% to 37% of total since 2018
item.description: The share of births to non-Maltese mothers rose from 24.45% of total births in 2018 to 37.26% in 2025, figures obtained by The Malta Independent show. Births to Maltese mothers fell from 3,393 to 2,755 while births to non-Maltese mothers increased from 1,098 to 1,636, leaving the overall number of births broadly stable at 4,391. Adjusted for the population of women of reproductive age, the total fertility rate fell from 1.23 to 0.99, with Maltese women still recording a higher rate than non-Maltese women.

item.title: Public spending on energy and fuel subsidies has more than doubled in the past year
item.description: Government figures show electricity subsidies rising from 133.5 million in 2025 to a projected 290 million in 2026, while spending to sustain fuel subsidies is up from 38.7 million to 85 million. Total energy and fuel subsidies are projected at about 400 million this year, taking the amount spent since the schemes were introduced four years ago to 1.35 billion. The figures come from the governments pre-budget consultation document and are attributed to higher costs linked to the international situation.

item.title: 199 academics and education staff demand repeal of fee hikes for non-EU nationals
item.description: Almost 200 academics and education staff across post-secondary and tertiary institutions urged the government to repeal fee increases targeting third-country nationals, describing the 2027 Budget measures as discriminatory and regressive. In a statement issued ahead of the Green Ribbon Project protest, the 199 signatories said the measures treat TCNs as indispensable economic engines while defining them socially and civically as disposable, and accused the government of creating an institutionalised, multi-tiered hierarchy of access to public services. The measures include steep increases in residence permit fees alongside a raft of new charges.

item.title: Climate change threatens Maltas tuna industry, 10-year plan warns
item.description: A proposed 10-year national aquaculture plan warns that rising sea temperatures could alter Atlantic bluefin tuna migration routes in the Mediterranean as early as 2030, threatening Maltas tuna fattening and export industry. The Action Plan for Sustainable Aquaculture 20262036, issued for public consultation, also flags higher risks of disease, parasites and mortality among captive tuna. The government proposes expanding fish farming further offshore and diversifying into new species while increasing production capacity.

item.title: Inquiry finds illegal electrical cable sparked the Salini fireworks factory blast
item.description: A magisterial inquiry into the 1 June explosion at the Ta Lourdes fireworks factory in Salini found that an illegal electrical cable, drawing power from a nearby farm under an informal arrangement in place for 26 years, ignited and set off a chain of blasts. Investigators estimated between eight and 11 tonnes of explosives were stored and manufactured irregularly on the site, with inspections failing to flag the breaches, and said a temporary extension lead buried in the ground had been installed in place of an armoured cable. The blast was felt kilometres away, damaged nearby homes and fields and destroyed the factory. The inquiry is expected to recommend criminal charges against several people.
